games.recap: Winners Bracket, Round 2, Series 4, Game 1 at Comerica Park. This booking forms the series in its archive slot: Detroit, the #4 seed, against Chicago, the #14 seed, the reseeded Winners Round 2 pairing, with Detroit home for Games 1, 2, 5 and 7. Booked from the master export file, played by Joe in the app: the report, the box score text, the full CSV block (linescore, batting, pitching, and fielding sections), the native PLAYS (JSON) rows, the graded play-by-play log with its manager decisions and decisions summary, and the full Rec JSON. Decisions: Ed Walsh takes the win for Chicago (5.2 IP, 24 BF, 5 H, 3 R, 2 ER, 1 BB, 1 SO, 1 HR). Hal Newhouser takes the loss for Detroit (6.1 IP, 29 BF, 6 H, 6 R, 6 ER, 5 BB, 9 SO, 2 HR): both Chicago home runs came off him. There is no save: Keith Foulke takes a hold in the Rec's extra line (1.1 IP, 4 BF, 0 H, 1 SO), entering in the bottom of the 6th with two inherited runners and stranding both (the Rec's extra line reads 2 inherited, 0 scored), and Eddie Cicotte pitched the last two innings, entering with a four-run lead so no save was available; he allowed Detroit's three-run 9th and finished the game. Scoring: Detroit scored first, Hank Greenberg's solo home run in the bottom of the 2nd. Chicago's four-run top of the 3rd decided it: Luke Appling tripled, Carlton Fisk walked, Eddie Collins singled Appling home, and Frank Thomas hit the three-run home run the export's summary names as the decisive play. Detroit answered in the bottom of the 3rd when Alan Trammell reached on Robin Ventura's one-base error and Ty Cobb doubled him home, the run unearned to Walsh, who is charged 3 runs against 2 earned; Cobb keeps the RBI. Chicago made it 5-2 in the top of the 4th (Ventura singled, Appling singled on the hit and run, Fisk walked, and Fielder Jones's forceout scored Ventura), and Detroit answered again in the bottom of the 4th (Greenberg doubled and Sam Crawford singled him home). Collins's solo home run in the top of the 7th made it 6-3. Chicago's 7th run, in the top of the 8th, is the game's only run without an RBI: Appling singled off Aurelio Lopez, took an extra base when Fisk struck out on the hit and run and Bill Freehan's throw went wild (E2), and scored on Lopez's wild pitch during Jones's walk (play row seq 67 carries 1 run and 0 RBI); Jones's printed RBI 1 is his top-of-the-4th forceout only, and Chicago's team RBI total is 6 against 7 runs. Detroit's bottom of the 9th nearly flipped the game: Freehan doubled, Trammell walked, and Charlie Gehringer hit a three-run home run off Cicotte to make it 7-6, but Al Kaline's single was followed by Greenberg's groundout to end it. Eddie Collins is the export's player of the game: 3 for 5 with the home run, 2 RBIs and 2 runs. Key lines: for Chicago, Appling 3 for 3 with a triple, a walk, 2 runs and a stolen base, Thomas 1 for 3 with the three-run home run and 2 walks, and Jones, Chicago's playing manager, 0 for 4 with a walk, the forceout RBI, and the walk during which the wild-pitch run scored; for Detroit, Greenberg 2 for 5 with a home run and a double and 2 runs, Gehringer 1 for 5 with the three-run home run, and Freehan 1 for 4 with a double and 11 putouts. The errors were Ventura's (E5, on Trammell's grounder in the 3rd) and Freehan's (E2, the wild throw in the 8th), one per club, carried in errors_by in the established shape; defensive lines booked in the established shape from the printed fielding section (Chicago 27 putouts and 10 assists, Frank Thomas 12 putouts; Detroit 27 putouts and 9 assists). Wild pitches: one each for Walsh and Lopez, Lopez's scoring Appling. Passed balls: none (Freehan's catching line reads PB 0, 1 stolen base against in 2 attempts, 1 caught stealing: Appling stole second and Minnie Miñoso was caught). No double plays were turned by either club, and no printed GIDP arises. Counting checks: Chicago plate appearances 43 (34 AB, 8 BB, 1 HBP) equal Detroit's 43 batters faced (Newhouser 29, Lopez 14); Detroit plate appearances 40 (36 AB, 4 BB) equal Chicago's 40 batters faced (Walsh 24, Foulke 4, Cicotte 12). Hit, walk, hit-by-pitch, home run and strikeout totals tie across the two boxes both ways. Earned runs: Chicago's staff is charged 5 earned runs against Detroit's 6 runs (Trammell's run unearned), and Detroit's staff 7 earned runs against Chicago's 7 (the wild-pitch run stays earned to Lopez). Manager grades: the grades list names both managers directly, so no label mapping is needed. Fielder Jones, who manages Chicago and also leads off for them, graded 7 decisions (3 paid off, 2 backfired, 2 neutral): four hit and runs at 1 paid off, 2 backfired and 1 neutral, both pitching changes (Foulke and Cicotte) paid off, and leaving a pitcher in neutral. Sparky Anderson graded 1 decision (0 paid off, 0 backfired, 1 neutral): the Lopez pitching change, neutral. Availability for Game 2 under the convention: Walsh (17 outs in this game) and Newhouser (19 outs) are unavailable; Cicotte (6 outs) and Lopez (8 outs) are capped at 3 outs; Foulke (4 outs) is free. Chicago leads the series 1-0. Managers: Fielder Jones (Chicago) and Sparky Anderson (Detroit). Venue is Comerica Park, as printed.

Winners Bracket, Round 2, Series 4, Game 2 at Comerica Park. Detroit wins 3-2 and ties the series 1-1. Booked from the master export file, played by Joe in the app: the report, the box score text, the full CSV block (linescore, batting, pitching, and fielding sections), the native PLAYS (JSON) rows, the graded play-by-play log with its manager decisions and decisions summary, and the full Rec JSON. Decisions: John Hiller takes the win for Detroit (1.0 IP, 3 BF, 0 H), a scoreless top of the 8th with the game tied. Dámaso Marte takes the loss for Chicago (0.1 IP, 4 BF, 2 H, 2 R, 2 ER, 1 BB, 1 SO, 1 HR) and is charged with the blown save in the Rec's extra line. Tommy Bridges takes the save (0.1 IP, 1 BF, 1 SO): he entered in the top of the 9th with two inherited runners, the tying run on second, and struck out Carlton Fisk to end the game; the Rec's extra line reads 2 inherited, 0 scored for him. Scoring: Detroit scored first, Charlie Gehringer's solo home run off Red Faber in the bottom of the 1st. Chicago tied it in the top of the 5th: Luke Appling doubled off Justin Verlander and Fielder Jones singled him home; Jones then stayed put on the steal call and Eddie Collins grounded into an inning-ending double play. Chicago took the lead in the top of the 6th: Frank Thomas singled, Minnie Miñoso bunted and reached when the lead runner was forced, Joe Jackson doubled, and, with Mike Henneman on in relief, Robin Ventura's groundout scored Miñoso; the run is charged to Verlander, and Henneman's inherited line in the Rec's extra line reads 2 inherited, 1 scored. Detroit won it in the bottom of the 8th off Marte: Al Kaline homered to tie the game, Hank Greenberg struck out, Miguel Cabrera walked, and Sam Crawford tripled Cabrera home, the decisive play the export's summary names. Hoyt Wilhelm came on and kept it at one run: Bill Freehan's fielder's choice cut Crawford down at home with the infield in, George Kell singled, and Alan Trammell grounded out; Wilhelm's inherited line reads 1 inherited, 0 scored. The top of the 9th: Willie Hernandez took the hold (0.2 IP, 4 BF, 1 H, 1 BB), giving up Ventura's single and Appling's walk before Bridges closed it. Sam Crawford is the export's player of the game: 3 for 3 with a double, the game-winning triple, an RBI and a walk. Key lines: for Detroit, Gehringer 1 for 4 with the home run, Kaline 1 for 4 with the tying home run, Kell 2 for 3 with a hit by pitch; for Chicago, Ventura 2 for 3 with an RBI and a walk, Appling 1 for 3 with a double, a run and a walk, Jackson 1 for 3 with a double. Pitching lines of note: Verlander 5.1 IP, 23 BF, 6 H, 2 ER, 1 BB, 1 SO and the game's only wild pitch, the top-of-the-1st third strike that Fielder Jones reached on (Jones struck out, beat the throw, was sacrificed to second and moved to third, and was stranded; the strikeout stands in his line, booked as printed). Faber started for Chicago (5.2 IP, 24 BF, 4 H, 1 ER, 1 BB, 2 SO, 1 HR, 2 HBP: Trammell in the 2nd and Kell in the 4th). Keith Foulke takes a hold in the Rec's extra line (1.1 IP, 5 BF, 1 H), entering in the bottom of the 6th with Crawford on second and stranding him (1 inherited, 0 scored). Henneman threw 1.2 scoreless innings for Detroit (5 BF, 1 SO). Errors: none, an errorless game for both clubs; the series' only errors remain Ventura's and Freehan's from Game 1. Double plays: Detroit turned one, Collins's top-of-the-5th grounder, a genuine double-play row in the log and the game's only printed GIDP. One GIDP difference does arise, on the rows' side: in the bottom of the 7th, Ty Cobb's forceout at second (Trammell forced, Cobb safe at first, row seq 58) is coded "DP 6-4-3" in the play rows although only one out was recorded on the play and the play log says no double play was turned; the rows rebuild Cobb with 1 GIDP against his printed 0. Under Joe's standing practice the play rows govern and the printed book line is unchanged; the difference is documented here and in the official record. Stolen bases: none, and nobody was caught stealing. Wild pitches: Verlander 1 (the Jones strikeout). Passed balls: none. Substitutes: Dick Allen pinch-hit for Jackson in the top of the 9th and flied out to left. Tony Phillips entered in the top of the 9th as a defensive replacement in left field for Crawford and never batted; he carries no batting line in the export and none is booked, and his fielding line (1 putout, Allen's flyout) is booked in the defense object exactly as the printed fielding section carries it. The defense object books putouts, assists and errors exactly as printed: Chicago 24 putouts and 12 assists (Frank Thomas 15 putouts, Appling 5 assists, Ventura 4 assists), Detroit 27 putouts and 18 assists (Greenberg 14 putouts, Trammell 5 assists, Gehringer 5 assists). Counting checks: Chicago plate appearances 36 (33 AB, 2 BB, 1 SH) equal Detroit's 36 batters faced (Verlander 23, Henneman 5, Hiller 3, Hernandez 4, Bridges 1); Detroit plate appearances 36 (32 AB, 2 BB, 2 HBP) equal Chicago's 36 batters faced (Faber 24, Foulke 5, Marte 4, Wilhelm 3). Hit, walk, hit-by-pitch, home run and strikeout totals tie across the two boxes both ways. Every run carries an RBI (Chicago 2 runs on 2 RBIs, Detroit 3 on 3), and both staffs' earned runs equal the runs (no unearned runs). Manager grades: the grades list names both managers directly, so no label mapping is needed. Fielder Jones graded 7 decisions (2 paid off, 5 backfired, 0 neutral): his three pitching changes went 2 paid off and 1 backfired (Marte in the 8th), and the sacrifice bunt in the 1st, the steal call in the 5th, the Allen pinch-hit in the 9th and his one hit and run all backfired. Sparky Anderson graded 6 decisions (4 paid off, 1 backfired, 1 neutral): four pitching changes at 3 paid off and 1 neutral, the Phillips defensive sub paid off, and his one hit and run backfired. Series graded totals through two games: Jones 14 decisions (5 paid off, 7 backfired, 2 neutral); Anderson 7 (4 paid off, 1 backfired, 2 neutral). Availability for Game 3 under the convention: Faber (17 outs in this game) and Verlander (16 outs) are unavailable; every other arm used is free (Foulke 4 outs, Marte 1, Wilhelm 2, Henneman 5, Hiller 3, Hernandez 2, Bridges 1, all under 6). Game 1's rest rules were honored in this game: Walsh and Newhouser sat, and Cicotte and Lopez, both capped at 3 outs, went unused. The series is tied 1-1. Managers: Fielder Jones (Chicago) and Sparky Anderson (Detroit). Venue is Comerica Park, as printed.

Winners Bracket, Round 2, Series 4, Game 3 at Guaranteed Rate Field. Detroit wins 10-9 and leads the series 2-1. Booked from the master export file, played by Joe in the app: the report, the box score text, the full CSV block (linescore, batting, pitching, and fielding sections), the native PLAYS (JSON) rows, the graded play-by-play log with its manager decisions and decisions summary, and the full Rec JSON. Decisions: Mickey Lolich takes the win for Detroit (6.0 IP, 34 BF, 13 H, 6 ER, 3 BB, 2 SO, 1 WP); he came back out for the bottom of the 7th and was charged with all three runs in it. Chris Sale takes the loss for Chicago (4.1 IP, 23 BF, 10 H, 7 ER, 3 SO, 3 HR allowed), knocked out in the top of the 5th. Aurelio Lopez takes the save (0.1 IP, 1 BF): he entered in the bottom of the 9th after Eddie Collins's two-run home run cut the lead to one, two out and the bases empty, and got Frank Thomas on a grounder to third to end the game; Sparky Anderson's pitching change to Lopez is graded paid off in the log. Scoring: Detroit scored four in the top of the 1st off Sale: Ty Cobb led off the game with a home run, the decisive play the export's summary names, Charlie Gehringer singled and took second on Al Kaline's groundout, Hank Greenberg struck out, and Miguel Cabrera singled Gehringer home, Sam Crawford doubled Cabrera home, and Bill Freehan singled Crawford home; George Kell singled and Alan Trammell flied out to end it. Chicago answered in the bottom of the 1st: Fielder Jones singled, Collins's groundout moved him to third, and Frank Thomas's sacrifice fly scored him; Minnie Miñoso doubled and Joe Jackson's infield single ended in a hidden-ball trick for the third out. Bottom of the 2nd: Luke Appling reached on Trammell's one-base error and never scored. Top of the 3rd: Greenberg homered off Sale (5-1). Bottom of the 3rd: Collins singled, took third on Thomas's hit-and-run single, and scored on Miñoso's single (5-2). Top of the 5th: Greenberg doubled and Cabrera's two-run home run made it 7-2 and finished Sale; against Dámaso Marte, Crawford reached on Miñoso's error in left, Freehan singled and Kell bunted them along, but Trammell grounded out and Crawford never scored. Bottom of the 5th: Collins singled off Lolich, stole second and took third on Freehan's wild throw, and scored on Thomas's clean single to right (7-3); the run is earned as printed, the error only advancing him. Top of the 6th, off Marte: two more, Cobb singled, Gehringer's hit-and-run single put runners at the corners, Kaline walked to load the bases, Greenberg walked to force in Cobb, Cabrera flied out, and Crawford's forceout grounder scored Gehringer (9-3). Bottom of the 7th: Lolich came back out and Chicago scored three: Thomas walked, Miñoso singled, Jackson doubled both home on the hit and run, Ventura walked, and Magglio Ordóñez's hit-and-run single scored Jackson. John Hiller then inherited two runners and struck out Carlton Fisk, the pinch-hitter Chet Lemon, and Collins with the bases loaded to end the inning; the Rec's extra line reads 2 inherited, 0 scored for Hiller, and he takes the hold. Bottom of the 8th: Hiller struck out Thomas and Miñoso, Jackson doubled, and Robin Ventura doubled him home (9-7); Willie Hernandez replaced Hiller with Ventura on second (1 inherited, 0 scored in the extra line) and Ordóñez popped out, and Hernandez takes the second hold. Top of the 9th: Freehan homered off Mark Buehrle (10-7), the insurance run that decided the game. Bottom of the 9th, traced from the play rows: Appling singled off Hernandez, Fisk popped out to short, Lemon forced Appling at second, and Collins homered to cut it to 10-9; Lopez came on for Hernandez and Thomas grounded out to third (Kell to Greenberg) to end it. Hank Greenberg is the export's player of the game: 2 for 4 with a double, the top-of-the-3rd home run, 2 RBIs, 2 runs and the bases-loaded walk. Key lines: for Detroit, Freehan 3 for 5 with the 9th-inning home run and 2 RBIs, Cabrera 2 for 5 with the two-run home run and 3 RBIs, Cobb 2 for 5 with the leadoff home run, Crawford 1 for 4 with a double and 2 RBIs, Gehringer 2 for 5 with 2 runs; for Chicago, Collins 3 for 6 with 3 runs, the 9th-inning two-run homer, a stolen base and 2 RBIs, Jackson 3 for 5 with two doubles and 2 RBIs, Miñoso 3 for 5 with a double and an RBI, Thomas 2 for 4 with 2 RBIs and the sacrifice fly, Ventura 2 for 4 with the 8th-inning RBI double. Pitching lines of note: Hiller 1.2 IP, 8 BF, 2 H, 1 ER, 1 BB, 5 SO and the hold, his only run Ventura's double; Hernandez 1.0 IP, 5 BF, 2 H, 2 ER, 1 HR and the hold despite the 9th-inning homer; Marte 2.2 IP, 15 BF, 4 H, 2 ER, 2 BB in relief of Sale; Buehrle 2.0 IP, 7 BF, 2 H, 1 ER, 2 SO, Freehan's homer his only run. Errors: Detroit 2 (Trammell in the 2nd, Freehan's throwing error in the 5th), Chicago 1 (Miñoso in the 5th); no run in the game was unearned: Appling never scored after reaching on Trammell's error, Collins's 5th-inning run scored on a clean single after Freehan's error only advanced him, and Crawford never scored after reaching on Miñoso's error, so both staffs' earned runs equal their runs exactly as printed. Double plays: Chicago turned one, Cabrera's top-of-the-8th grounder, a genuine double-play row in the log and the game's only printed GIDP. Stolen bases: Collins and Carlton Fisk, both off Freehan (his catching line reads SB against 2, CS 0, PB 0). Wild pitches: Lolich 1. Passed balls: none. Hit by pitch: none on either side. Substitutes: Chet Lemon pinch-hit for Jones in the bottom of the 7th, struck out, and stayed in the game in center field; he caught Trammell's 9th-inning flyout and forced Appling at second in the bottom of the 9th. Tony Phillips replaced Sam Crawford in left field before the bottom of the 8th and batted in his spot in the top of the 9th, flying out to left; he carries no fielding line in the export and none is booked. The defense object books putouts, assists and errors exactly as printed: Detroit 27 putouts and 9 assists (Greenberg 10 putouts; Gehringer 4 assists, Kell 4 assists), Chicago 27 putouts and 6 assists (Thomas 7 putouts, Fisk 6 putouts and 1 assist, Ventura 3 assists). Counting checks: Detroit plate appearances 45 (42 AB, 2 BB, 1 SH) equal Chicago's 45 batters faced (Sale 23, Marte 15, Buehrle 7); Chicago plate appearances 48 (43 AB, 4 BB, 1 SF) equal Detroit's 48 batters faced (Lolich 34, Hiller 8, Hernandez 5, Lopez 1). Hit, walk, home run and strikeout totals tie across the two boxes both ways. Every run carries an RBI (Detroit 10 runs on 10 RBIs, Chicago 9 on 9). One correction to the booking brief, booked as printed: the brief carried Joe Jackson with one double; the export's CSV batting section, its Rec bat array and the play rows (the bottom-of-the-7th double and a bottom-of-the-8th double to right) all show two, and two are booked. Manager grades: the grades list names both managers directly, so no label mapping is needed. Fielder Jones graded 13 decisions (6 paid off, 2 backfired, 5 neutral): six hit and runs at 3 paid off, 1 backfired and 2 neutral, two pitching changes at 1 paid off and 1 neutral, two steals at 1 paid off and 1 neutral, two left-pitcher-in calls at 1 paid off and 1 neutral, and the Lemon pinch-hit backfired. Sparky Anderson graded 5 decisions (4 paid off, 1 backfired, 0 neutral): all three pitching changes paid off (Hiller in the 7th, Hernandez in the 8th, Lopez in the 9th), his one hit and run paid off, and the Phillips defensive sub backfired. Series graded totals through three games: Jones 27 decisions (11 paid off, 9 backfired, 7 neutral); Anderson 12 (8 paid off, 2 backfired, 2 neutral). Availability for Game 4 under the convention: Lolich (18 outs in this game) and Sale (13 outs) are unavailable; Marte (8 outs) and Buehrle (6 outs) are capped at 3 outs; Hiller (5 outs), Hernandez (3) and Lopez (1) are free. Game 2's rest rules were honored in this game: Faber and Verlander sat. Managers: Fielder Jones (Chicago) and Sparky Anderson (Detroit). Venue is Guaranteed Rate Field, as printed.

Winners Bracket, Round 2, Series 4, Game 4 at Guaranteed Rate Field. Detroit wins 6-5 and leads the series 3-1. Winners Bracket, Round 2, Series 4, Game 5 at Comerica Park. Detroit wins the series 4-1 and advances on the winners side; Chicago drops to the losers bracket with its first series loss. Chicago won Game 1 (7-6); Detroit won Game 2 (3-2), Game 3 (10-9) and Game 4 (6-5). Booked from the master export file, played by Joe in the app: the report, the box score text, the full CSV block (linescore, batting, pitching, fielding sections), the full Rec with its bat/pit/fld/grades/extra arrays, the native PLAYS JSON rows, and the narrative play log. The game export was cross-checked against the series master export: the two Game 5 Recs agree in every field. One line was booked as printed where the booking brief differed: Robin Ventura is carried with 1 RBI and no hit by pitch, as the export's CSV section, Rec array and play log all print (his second-inning groundout scored Chicago's only run); the brief had carried no RBI and one hit by pitch. Fielder Jones managed Chicago but did not play; Chet Lemon led off and played center field. Detroit scored two in the 1st: Cobb walked, Gehringer lined into a double play on the hit and run, Kaline doubled, Greenberg's single to right scored Kaline (the Report's decisive play), and Cabrera's double to center scored Greenberg. Chicago's only run came in the 2nd: Jackson tripled to right and Ventura's groundout scored him. Detroit broke it open in the 3rd: Kaline walked, Crawford singled, and Freehan's double to left scored both; Kell's single scored Freehan, and after Trammell singled, Cobb's single scored Kell to make it 6-1 and finish Buehrle. Marte inherited two runners and stranded both, Wilhelm threw a scoreless 5th, and Foulke took the last three innings: Cabrera homered off him in the 6th, and in the 8th Cobb singled and stole second, Gehringer's single scored him, Kaline hit a two-run home run, and after Cabrera singled, Freehan's two-run home run made it 12-1. Bridges went the distance: nine innings, 36 batters faced, five hits, one earned run, six walks, two strikeouts. Detroit's hits were spread through the order: Cabrera went 4 for 5 with a double and a home run, Cobb 3 for 4 with a steal, Trammell 3 for 4 with a double, and Freehan, the player of the game, drove in four with a double and a home run. Chicago managed five hits off Bridges, Jackson's triple the only extra-base hit besides Thomas's double. Availability from Game 4 was honored: Morris, Lyons and Jenks, all unavailable, did not appear.
